title: Proper flat geometrically reduced connected fibres have universal structure-sheaf pushforward
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base] of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. If for every point $s\in S$, with residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field], the fibre $X_s$ is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected over $\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] (that is, the geometric fibres of $f$ are reduced and connected), then $f_*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_S$, and this isomorphism remains true after every base change $T\to S$ [def-pc-base-change].

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.32.1, Tag 0E0L

proof.text: Apply the fibrewise criterion [lem-sc-proper-flat-global-sections-criterion] to $f$. Its proper, flat and finite-presentation hypotheses are exactly those in the statement. For each $s\in S$, the fibre $X_s$ is proper over $\kappa(s)$ (properness is stable under base change), and by hypothesis it is geometrically reduced and geometrically connected over $\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Therefore [lem-pc-h0-geom-connected], applied over the field $\kappa(s)$, identifies the canonical map $\kappa(s)\to H^0(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ with an isomorphism.

proof.text: The criterion now gives $f_*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_S$, and its universal base-change clause gives the same isomorphism after every morphism $T\to S$.
